methods.label: Count equally likely parity patterns
methods.explanation:
Only whether each integer is even or odd matters. Among the integers from \(0\) through \(2007\), there are \(1004\) even numbers and \(1004\) odd numbers. Because the four choices are independent, their \(2^4=16\) parity patterns are equally likely.

Write \(E\) for even and \(O\) for odd. For the ordered pair \((a,d)\), the four patterns are
\[
(E,E),\ (E,O),\ (O,E),\ (O,O).
\]
The first three make \(ad\) even, and only the last makes it odd. The same counts apply to \((b,c)\).

The difference \(ad-bc\) is even exactly when the two products have the same parity. There are \(3\cdot3=9\) patterns making both products even and \(1\cdot1=1\) making both odd. These cases are disjoint and include every way to obtain an even difference. Pairing the two factor patterns specifies all four parities uniquely, so there is no double counting.

The required probability is
\[
\frac{9+1}{16}=\boxed{\frac58},
\]
choice \(\text{E}\).
